doctrine:
CONSOLIDATED DOCTRINE: Adobe Creative Suite Tutorial Corpus (122 segments)

SCOPE: Video tutorial transcripts spanning Photoshop compositing, Lightroom culling, Adobe Firefly AI, and Premiere Pro editing. Primary value is concrete technique sequences for non-destructive post-production workflows. No strategic/business doctrine. Applicable to SNIPED post-production and Track B AI creative work.

---

PHOTOSHOP COMPOSITING DOCTRINE

Foundational rules:
- Non-destructive-first: smart objects + adjustment layers + masks. Never merge/rasterize without a copy. Eraser tool is banned; use layer masks instead.
- Layer mask rule: mask-inversion (ALT+click mask to view mask channel directly) is the fastest diagnostic for edge bleed.
- Selection-before-generative mandate: always create/refine a selection before invoking generative fill. Sloppy selections produce context-aware hallucinations.
- Smart objects preserve quality through scale transforms; rasterize only at final output.

Layer type taxonomy (7 types to know):
1. Pixel layers (base content)
2. Smart Object layers (non-destructive, linkable)
3. Adjustment layers (curves, color balance, hue/sat, levels)
4. Fill layers (solid color, gradient, pattern)
5. Type layers
6. Shape layers
7. Group layers

Blend mode selection rules:
- Multiply: darken composites, shadow overlays, burn in detail
- Screen: lighten, glow, spark/particle overlay
- Soft Light: contrast boost without full Overlay harshness; mid-tone sculpting
- Overlay: high-contrast texture burn; use sparingly
- Luminosity: color grading layers where you want tonal shift without hue bleed
- ALT+click blend-if sliders to split the tonal range; softens harsh compositing transitions

Depth-of-field layering hierarchy (poster/composite assembly order):
1. Background (sky/environment, lowest resolution blur)
2. Mid-ground elements (moderate sharpness)
3. Subject layer (sharpest, masks tightest)
4. Foreground overlay (atmospheric: particles, fog, film grain, chromatic abberation vignette)
5. Color/grade adjustment layers stacked above all

Shadow and ambient construction:
- Shadow under subject: new layer set to Multiply, low-opacity (15-30%) soft brush, desaturated or dark warm tone
- Particle/ambient dust: custom scatter brush, screen mode, 20-40% opacity, size jitter + scatter randomized
- Brush creation for particles: define from pixel layer, set scatter/size jitter in brush settings panel

Color grading stack order (adjustment layers, top to bottom = last applied first):
1. Curves (primary tonal contrast + channel-by-channel RGB)
2. Color Balance (shadow/midtone/highlight color push)
3. Hue/Saturation (selective desaturation; skin-safe by protecting orange range)
4. Photo Filter or Solid Color fill in luminosity/color mode (final color cast)
Rule of thumb: shadows push cold (blue-cyan), highlights push warm (yellow-orange) for cinematic separation.

Dark/horror poster specific workflow (Stranger Things / dark editorial aesthetic):
- Start with curves to crush blacks
- Blend subject on background using luminosity blend-if to drop bright halos
- Add chromatic aberration: duplicate layer, shift red channel left, blue channel right, reduce opacity
- Film grain: Filter > Noise > Add Noise (Gaussian, Monochromatic, 2-4%)
- Vignette via solid color fill layer (black), blend Multiply, apply gradient mask radial center-to-edge

Channel-based oil painting hack (unusual but functional):
- Duplicate layer, go to Channels panel, run Filter > Stylize > Oil Paint on individual channels, recombine; produces painterly texture without full rasterization commitment.

Curves mastery rules:
- S-curve for contrast without destroying blacks or blowing highlights
- Camera Raw curves and Photoshop curves are NOT identical: Camera Raw applies before pixel rendering; Photoshop curves apply on top of rendered data. Do not assume parity between the two.
- Per-channel curve editing is more precise than RGB master curve for color correction

Dodge and Burn:
- Create empty layer, fill 50% gray, set to Overlay; paint white (dodge) and black (burn) with soft brush at 5-15% opacity. This is non-destructive manual dodging.

Frequency Separation:
- High-frequency layer (texture): Apply Image from low to high at 200% Subtract, Linear Light blend mode
- Low-frequency layer (color/tone): Gaussian blur at skin pore radius (~3-6px for typical portrait)
- Retouch tone on low, texture on high; never cross-contaminate

Liquify tool ethics gate:
- Forward Warp: ~90% of liquify use cases (clothing fit, hair flyaways, fabric wrinkles)
- BANNED: body shape editing on client deliverables (waist, arms, legs)
- SNIPED gate: liquify for garment and hair fixes ONLY; document this in retoucher brief

Clone Stamp operating settings:
- Hardness: 0-15% for skin/blend areas; 50-70% for edge-defined repair
- Pressure/flow: 30-50% for gradual buildup
- Show Overlay (beta): enables see-through clone preview before committing
- Always sample from adjacent area at same light angle

---

ADOBE FIREFLY / GENERATIVE AI INTEGRATION DOCTRINE

Firefly Image 5 specs:
- Max resolution: 4MP output
- Credit cost: standard generation 10 credits; partner models (Nano Banana 2: 10-40 credits; Pro partner models: 40 credits)
- Remove/distraction tool: currently free (0 credits) as of series recording date
- Model picker: available in UI; select by generation goal

Model selection decision rule:
- Firefly native model: use when facial detail preservation is critical (client headshots, identity retention)
- Partner/artistic models: use for creative/abstract/texture-heavy work where identity accuracy is lower priority
- Anti-pattern: using partner model on any deliverable where the subject's face must be accurate

Generative Fill operating rules:
- Make a clean selection first; the tool reads selection context to understand what to replace
- Extend canvas workflow: extend canvas via crop tool, select new blank area, generative fill with blank prompt for seamless extension
- Generative expand (subject-aware crop extension): use when subject is too tightly framed; generates contextually matched background

New tools in Photoshop 2026 / Firefly pipeline:
- Rotate Object: AI-based 3D rotation of product/object in scene; preserves lighting direction
- Harmonize: adjusts subject tone/color to match background after composite paste
- Layer Cleanup AI (beta): detects and trims excess transparent pixels on layer; non-destructive
- Dynamic text shapes: text that flows into and around shape paths automatically
- General Distractions Removal: content-aware batch removal (power lines, stray objects); applied via filter
- Reflection Removal: dedicated tool for window/glass reflections
- Firefly Boards: mood board / asset collection surface inside Firefly web app

Remove tool vs Patch tool decision:
- Remove tool: fast AI removal for isolated distractions; no manual source selection needed
- Patch tool: use when remove produces hallucination artifacts; manually define source patch area

---

LIGHTROOM CULLING WORKFLOW DOCTRINE

5-Star system for culling:
- 5 stars: hero selects (delivery candidates)
- 4 stars: backup selects (client choice overflow)
- 3 stars: technically acceptable (hold)
- 1-2 stars: outtake (reject but not delete immediately)
- Compare view (C key): toggle between two candidates for side-by-side elimination
Batch flag workflow: flag then filter, not rate-then-batch-export; reduces miss rate.

---

PREMIERE PRO OPERATING DOCTRINE

Color correction vs color grading distinction:
- Color correction: fix what is broken (wrong white balance, clipped exposure, color cast from source). Done first.
- Color grading: build aesthetic on top of corrected footage. Done after correction is complete.
- S-curve strategy for footage grading: lift shadows slightly, pull highlights slightly for compressed, filmic contrast.

Audio delivery standards:
- Loudness metering: target platform specs (-14 LUFS integrated for YouTube/Spotify; -16 LUFS for podcast distribution)
- Dynamics processing: compression ratio 2:1 to 4:1 for spoken word; limiter at -1 dBFS true peak

Title/lower-third animation formula:
- In point: position + opacity keyframes (ease in from below/side)
- Hold: static for legibility window (minimum 2 seconds for 3-word titles)
- Out point: fast scale or opacity fade

AI masking in Premiere:
- Apply Mask > AI tracking for subject isolation in video; re-evaluate mask every 5-10 seconds for drift correction

Keyboard efficiency:
- J/K/L: reverse/pause/forward playback speed
- I/O: in and out points
- M: marker
- Ctrl+K (Win) / Cmd+K (Mac): cut at playhead

---

SCRIPT WRITING FRAMEWORK (from segments 61-70, video course content)

5-Step Script Framework:
1. Psychology: define the emotional state you want the audience to feel at the end before writing a word
2. Packaging: hook, title, thumbnail concept locked before script
3. Outline: beats and transitions roughed (not sentences)
4. Intro: first 30 seconds must deliver the hook promise and proof of credibility
5. Body + Outro: deliver on promise; outro = CTA + next-video bridge

First 10 Pages principle (screenplay craft, applicable to content structure):
- The first 10 pages (or equivalent opening segment) must establish world, protagonist desire, and dramatic question. Failure to establish all three = audience drop.

48-hour screenplay sprint methodology:
- Day 1: outline only (no prose). Beat sheet complete by end of day.
- Day 2: write forward, never backward. No revising previous scenes until first pass complete. Velocity over quality on sprint.

Automation workflow (AI video pipeline note from seg 61-70):
- Stack: Nan + Sora + Google Sheets + webhooks
- Use case: batch AI video generation driven by spreadsheet inputs with webhook triggers
- Applicable to SNIPED Track B AI volume production if pursued

---

CROSS-CUTTING OPERATING RULES

1. Non-destructive mandate: every layer operation preserves original. Smart objects, adjustment layers, masks. No destructive merges during creative phase.
2. Selection discipline: always refine selection before any generative or content-aware operation.
3. Blend mode literacy: know the 6 primary blend modes and when each applies (see above).
4. Ethics gate: liquify for garment/hair ONLY on client deliverables; no body shape editing.
5. Model selection: Firefly native for face-critical work; partner models for creative/abstract.
6. Color pipeline sequence: correction first, grading second, never reversed.
7. Frequency separation: tone and texture on separate layers; never cross-contaminate.
8. Reject gate: any automated output (generative fill, remove tool, harmonize) must be visually compared against source before accepting. Failed cleanup artifacts are worse than leaving source context.

---

WHAT IS NOT IN THIS DOCUMENT
- No business strategy
- No pricing logic
- No client communication frameworks
- No SNIPED OS operating rules
- No distribution or audience-building doctrine

SCOPE BOUNDARY: This corpus is a post-production tooling reference. Its doctrine applies to: (a) Photoshop compositing and retouching, (b) Lightroom culling, (c) Firefly AI integration, (d) Premiere Pro editing and color, (e) script/content structure for video. Route to this doc only when making tool decisions or workflow decisions in those domains.
